chunks: And this does not contradict what Al-As ibn al-Qasim narrated, saying:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about visiting [the Prophet's tomb] after the Hajj pilgrimage during the days of Tashriq, and he said, 'No.' Because the meaning within it is that staying in Mina is superior, and although visiting is permissible, what has been narrated indicates this:

key_terms.أَيَّامِ التَّشْرِيقِ: The days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.الزِّيَارَةِ: Visitation (specifically to the Prophet's tomb or shrines)
key_terms.بِمِنًى: In Mina (the site of the stoning of the pillars and staying during Hajj)
key_terms.زِيَارَةِ الْحَجِّ: The visitation associated with the Hajj pilgrimage

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to visit the Prophet's tomb after Hajj during the days of Tashriq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the hierarchy of virtues during the days of Tashriq, ruling that while visiting the Prophet’s tomb is permissible, remaining in Mina for the prescribed stay is superior. The apparent contradiction is resolved by understanding that the 'No' refers to the preference for not leaving Mina rather than a prohibition of the visit itself, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing ritual obligations with recommended acts (mustahabbat).
